hints: Focus on what Z could be, since chlorine reacting with NaOH by disproportionation only gives two possible oxychlorine products.
Calculate the % by mass of oxygen in $\text{NaClO}$ and in $\text{NaClO}_3$ and see which matches 45.1%.
Link your identified product to its preparation conditions, remembering cold dilute favours the +1 state while hot concentrated pushes oxidation further to +5.
walkthrough:
**Recall the two possible disproportionation products**

Chlorine with NaOH undergoes disproportionation to $\text{Cl}^-$ and an oxychlorate. There are only two common Z candidates here.

Cold dilute: $$2\text{NaOH} + \text{Cl}_2 \rightarrow \text{NaClO} + \text{NaCl} + \text{H}_2\text{O}$$
Hot concentrated: $$6\text{NaOH} + 3\text{Cl}_2 \rightarrow \text{NaClO}_3 + 5\text{NaCl} + 3\text{H}_2\text{O}$$

**Use % oxygen to identify Z**

Z contains Na, Cl and O, so test $\text{NaClO}$ ($\text{Cl}$ is +1) and $\text{NaClO}_3$ ($\text{Cl}$ is +5).

For $\text{NaClO}$: $$M_r = 23.0 + 35.5 + 16.0 = 74.5$$ $$\% \text{O} = \frac{16.0}{74.5} \times 100 = 21.5\%$$
For $\text{NaClO}_3$: $$M_r = 23.0 + 35.5 + (3 \times 16.0) = 106.5$$ $$\% \text{O} = \frac{48.0}{106.5} \times 100 = 45.1\%$$

**Assign oxidation state and conditions**

The 45.1% match tells us Z is $\text{NaClO}_3$. Let the oxidation state of Cl be $x$.
$$+1 + x + 3(-2) = 0$$
$$x = +5$$
Since chlorate(V) is formed, hot concentrated NaOH must have been used.

options.A: Cold dilute NaOH with +1 is the recipe for $\text{NaClO}$, sodium chlorate(I). Its oxygen percentage is only about 21.5%, not 45.1%, so it cannot be Z.
options.B: Cold dilute NaOH does not give the +5 state. This mixes the conditions for $\text{NaClO}$ with the oxidation state for $\text{NaClO}_3$, so the row is inconsistent.
options.C: Hot concentrated NaOH does not give the +1 state. This mixes the conditions for $\text{NaClO}_3$ with the oxidation state for $\text{NaClO}$, so the row is inconsistent.
options.D: Hot concentrated NaOH gives $\text{NaClO}_3$ by disproportionation. Its calculated % O is 45.1% and Cl has oxidation state +5, matching all the data for Z.
